REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - APRIL 9, 2015 - CITY HALL -
7:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
APRIL 9, 2015 IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin T. Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Boy Scout Troop 693.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair George Ray
  Mayor/Chair Carol Chen

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Presentations were made as follows:

  Autism Society (50th Anniversary)

  Lawrence Dang (Eagle Scout)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Chris Foster, resident, thanked the Council and staff for the Adaptive Recreation
  program.

  Morris Satki, resident, spoke regarding tree trimming.

  Merri Wheaton, resident spoke regarding the Annual Cerritos Prayer Breakfast.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one
  motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency
  Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be removed from the
  Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated
  April 9, 2015 (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  April 9, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Ray, to approve the Register of
  Demands dated April 9, 2015 in the total amount of $2,940,375.66 (COUNCIL). The
  motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency dated
  April 9, 2015 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Ray, to approve the Register of
  Demands dated April 9, 2015 in the total amount of $8,209.07 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  March 26, 2015 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Ray, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of March 26, 2015
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending February 28, 2015
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Ray, to approve the Treasurer’s
  Reports for the period ending February 28, 2015 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.
 City of Cerritos  April 9, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Heritage Park Shelter
  Replacement, Project No. 12794, Bid No. 1204-15 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Ray, to:
  1. Authorize the use of available funds in the Project No. 10073 account for Project No.
  12794; and
  2. Award a contract in the amount of $124,217 for Heritage Park Shelter Replacement,
  Project No. 12794, Bid No. 1204-15, to RE Schultz and reject all other bids; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders, including a change order for the removal of the Auto Square gazebo.
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of various agreements and the revised environmental
  notice of determination for the expansion of the Cerritos recycled water system
  to serve Forest Lawn Memorial Park in the City of Cypress (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to:
  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the revised design funding agreement with
  Forest Lawn Memorial Park for costs associated with the expansion of the
  Cerritos Recycled Water System; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the construction funding agreement with
  Forest Lawn Memorial Park for costs associated with the expansion of the Cerritos
  Recycled Water System; and
  3. Receive and file the revised Environmental Notice of Determination; and
  4. Approve the plans and specifications for the construction phase of the project; and
  5. Authorize staff to issue bid documents and specifications for the construction phase of
  the project. and
  6. Ensure that hard copies of the report are available at City Hall for the public’s review
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  April 9, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  Review and consideration of an implementation agreement with the Gateway City
  Council of Governments for the preparation of an Artesia Boulevard Corridor
  Study (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Hal Arbogast, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Gateway Cities Council of Governments
  Implementation Agreement with the approved change as designated in the staff
  report as Exhibit 1, and in a form approved by the City Attorney; and
  2. Appropriate $41,501.25 from Proposition A funds for the City’s share of the total
  study cost (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  An informational report on tree trimming and sidewalk repairs for Fiscal Year
  2014-2015 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Hal Arbogast, Director of Public Works.  A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Paul Bellenbaum, resident, commented regarding trees.

  Noting there were no futher individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to receive and file the
  report. The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
 City of Cerritos  April 9, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

10.  Legislative Items (continued)

10B1. Review and consideration of support for (State Legislation) Senate Bill 485 which
  will allow the Sanitation Districts of Los Angeles County (LACSD)to assist cities in
  achieving compliance with municipal storm water requirements through
  collaboration among existing local agencies in Los Angeles County (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to direct staff to prepare
  letters of support for Senate Bill 485 to the following: Senator Ed Hernandez, Senate
  Committee on Rules, Senator Tony Mendoza, Assembly Member Christina Garcia,
  League of California Cities, California Contract Cities, Gateway City Council of
  Governments, Independent Cities Association and Gonsalves and Son (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Solanki, Pulido and Edwards, and Mayor
  Pro Tem Ray, and Mayor Chen.

  CONSENSUS (Ray): Directed staff to bring back to the next meeting a review of the
  proposed tree ordinance brought to Council last year.

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Directed staff to bring back to Council within 30 days a
  recommendation for a community assessment survey or program to gather input from
  residents and the business community on current City issues.

  Name of Case: Water Replenishment District of Southern California v. City of
  Cerritos
  Los Angeles Superior Court Case No. VC060498
 City of Cerritos  April 9, 2015
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6
12.  Closed Session (continued)

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session to discuss Items 12A & 12B.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:24 p.m. in memory of Dr. John Hom.
